cards.explanation: The answer is a new heaven and a new earth. John says, “Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth…” because the first heaven and earth had passed away. I know a little about fresh starts. One night I'm in the back of a junk drawer, and next thing I know an angel has me standing on a cookie planet. But this new is heaven AND earth, friends, so mine looks small.

The answer is as a bride adorned for her husband. John says the city is prepared “…as a bride adorned for her husband.” That fits my work nicely, since the Supper I'm baking for is a marriage supper (Revelation 19:9). I'm not saying I cried into the dough, but the dough is a little salty. A wedding is the picture, friends.

The answer is True. The loud voice from the throne says, “Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man, and He will dwell with them.” God Himself, right there with His people. I'll be honest, friends, this verse makes my mustache stand straight up.

The answer is “former.” The voice says there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, “…for the former things have passed away.” The old things are done, and that's why those four go with them. I love how plain that is. Short line, huge news.

The answer is “new.” The One seated on the throne is the one speaking, and He says, “Behold, I make all things new.” ALL things, friends. Not some things, not just the top shelf, ALL. I'm a stamper who got made new, so I'm a little biased, but that might be my favorite line in the whole passage.

The answer is that these words are faithful and true. The One on the throne says, “Write this down, for these words are faithful and true.” He gives the reason Himself, so we don't have to guess. I write down my recipes, and half of them just say 'more chips.' These words are on a whole different level.

The answer is the thirsty. The One on the throne says, “To the thirsty I will give freely from the spring of the water of life.” Freely, friends. That means given, not sold. I have been thirsty for less than this.

The answer is False, and the real promise is a big one. The One on the throne says, “The one who overcomes will inherit all things…” All things, friends, not a sliver. Then He adds, “…I will be his God, and he will be My son.” That's the best part of the promise.

The answer is the cowardly and unbelieving and all liars. This part is heavy, so I'll say it plain. He says, “…and all liars, their place will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur.” The list starts with the cowardly and unbelieving, and it names more than that. Then He says, “This is the second death.”

The answer is the glory of God. The city is “…shining with the glory of God.” Later John says the glory of God illuminates the city (Revelation 21:23). No need for a bulb or a box. My stars come from finished cookie boxes, but this city needs none.
The answer is True. The city has “…twelve gates inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel…” Twelve gates, twelve names. I didn't even have to carry the one.

The answer is apostles. “The wall of the city had twelve foundations bearing the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.” Jesus chose twelve of His disciples and called them apostles (Luke 6:13). So the tribes' names are on the gates, and the apostles' names are on the foundations. That's a lot of names for one wall, friends.

The answer is that the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple. John says there's no temple “…because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple.” The Lamb is Jesus (John 1:29). So there's no building to point at. The temple is Them, and I think that's about the best thing a city could have.

The answer is lamp. John says, “…the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp.” The Lamb is Jesus (John 1:29). So the light comes from God's glory and from the Lamb. Sun and moon can take the day off, friends.

The answer is the nations. John says, “By its light the nations will walk, and into it the kings of the earth will bring their glory.” The nations walk by the city's light, and the kings bring their glory in. I think that's a lot of people on one street, friends. The street is pure gold, so it'll look good.

The answer is False, friends. John says, “Its gates will never be shut at the end of the day, because there will be no night there.” No night, so no closing time. I have a CLOSED sign in my bakery, and this city doesn't need one.

The answer is those whose names are written in the Lamb's Book of Life. The verse says, “…only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.” The Lamb is Jesus (John 1:29). It's about whose names are written down. That's the whole answer, and I love how clear it is.

The answer is throne. The river is “…flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb.” So the water of life starts right at the throne. The Lamb is Jesus (John 1:29). I'd follow that river upstream any day, friends.

The answer is life. On either side of the river stands a tree of life. And that tree has twelve kinds of fruit and a fresh crop each month. A tree that gives a fresh crop every month is my kind of kitchen. I'd just keep walking back to it.
The answer is False. The tree is “…bearing twelve kinds of fruit and yielding a fresh crop for each month.” A fresh crop every month, not once a year. My ovens would be jealous, friends.

The answer is any curse. John says, “No longer will there be any curse.” None at all, friends. And the throne of God and of the Lamb will be within the city, so His servants are worshiping Him right there. That's a good place to be.
The answer is True. John says, “They will see His face, and His name will be on their foreheads.” God's servants will see His face. I've been waiting a good while to hear a line like that, friends.

The answer is forever and ever. John says, “…they will reign forever and ever.” No end date at all. I've been given a lot of deadlines in my day, and this is the first line that doesn't have one. Forever and ever, friends.
